newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives - EMU conditions unlikely to be met.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives - EMU conditions unlikely to be met.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives said in their election manifesto on Wednesday it was "very unlikely" there would be sufficient convergence of economic conditions for a European single currency to proceed "safely" in 1999.
It also said it would not include legislation on the European Union single currency in the first Queen's Speech of a new Conservative government after the May 1 election.

"It is in our national interest to take part in the (EMU) negotiations," the manifesto said. "Not to do so would be an abdication of responsibility. A single currency would affect us whether we were in or out."

The manifesto added: "On the information currently available we believe that it is very unlikely that there will be sufficient convergence of economic conditions across Europe for a single currency to proceed safely on the target date of January 1, 1999."
The manifesto if EMU could not proceed safely it would be better for Europe to delay introduction of the Euro "rather than rush ahead to meet an artificial timetable".
